   **My first call if the injury is substantial or liability looks complicated.**

2. **Johnston Withers Lawyers** — specifically handles slip-and-fall/public-liability cases and offers no-win-no-fee arrangements. It's also in Doyle's 2026 “Recommended” group. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-law-firms-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[johnstonwithers.com.au](https://johnstonwithers.com.au/what-we-do/personal-injury-lawyers/public-liability-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

3. **Paul Alvaro Lawyers** — particularly relevant because the firm expressly handles **slip-and-fall claims against shopping centres involving multiple parties**. Paul Alvaro has decades of personal-injury experience, and the firm has repeatedly appeared in Doyle's public-liability rankings. 4. **C+F Lawyers** — another current Doyle's “Leading” firm for plaintiff public liability in SA. 5. **MKF Personal Injury Lawyers Adelaide** — also currently “Leading” in Doyle's, with a dedicated public-liability practice covering slips, trips and falls. It offers a free claim check and no-win-no-fee arrangements. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-law-firms-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**TGB is another very strong option.** Tindall Gask Bentley Lawyers is in Doyle's 2026 Leading group and specifically deals with shopping-centre falls, including investigating CCTV, witnesses and medical evidence. It offers a free initial consultation and no-win-no-fee options, subject to conditions. [tgb.com.au](https://tgb.com.au/public-liability-claims-in-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What I'd do in your situation

Don't accept a settlement or sign anything from the shopping centre/insurer before speaking to a lawyer. Evidence such as **CCTV footage and witness details can disappear**, so it's worth acting promptly. [wpilawyers.com.au](https://wpilawyers.com.au/practice-areas/injury-compensation-lawyers/public-liability-claims/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Also, a fall by itself doesn't necessarily establish liability—you generally need to establish negligence and resulting loss. In SA, court proceedings for these claims generally have a **3-year limitation period**, although exceptions can apply. [tgb.com.au](https://tgb.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/injured-in-a-public-place-what-you-need-to-know-about-public-liability-claims-in-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
